sentences.text: Zuul is an extinct herbivorous ankylosaurine dinosaur belonging to the family Ankylosauridae and the subfamily Ankylosaurinae.
This species is the first ankylosaurine known from both a complete skull and a complete tail club, with a skull measuring about 50 centimeters long.
Its skull featured a wide, flat snout that was cut off at the front, and the armor tiles on its head overlapped and pointed upward.
The animal was estimated to reach a total length of six meters and weigh approximately 2.5 tons.
The tail itself measured 278 centimeters in total length.
Zuul holds the record for the longest tail club shaft among North American ankylosaurids, measuring 210 centimeters including the handle.
Fossil remains of keratinous scales like those found on Zuul are extremely rare.
As of 2017, the Zuul specimen was the most complete ankylosaur found in the Judith River Formation.
The holotype was discovered in 2014 near Havre, Montana, when a truck carrying a twelve-meter-high load accidentally struck a tail club of an ankylosaur.
The skeleton was found lying on its back in a rotated position after a loader hit the club while removing earth.
The find occurred in the Judith River Formation, specifically the middle Coal Ridge Member, though by 2017 only the tail had been prepared for study.
Researchers suggest that Zuul used its tail club to smash the lower legs of attacking predators as a defensive tactic.
The genus Zuul and the species Zuul crurivastator were named by Arbour and Evans in 2017, identifying it as an Ankylosaurini within the subfamily Ankylosaurinae.
Zuul forms a clade with Ankylosaurus, Anodontosaurus, Dyoplosaurus, and Scolosaurus, and in nine of the ten most parsimonious trees recovered, it is the sister group to Dyoplosaurus.
Zuul lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 75 million years ago, in what is now North America.

The phylogenetic analysis of Zuul yielded inconclusive results regarding the exact interrelationships of ankylosaurins, largely influenced by the placement of Anodontosaurus and Ziapelta. Phylogenetic trees recovered for Zuul show nine out of ten place it as the sister group of Dyoplosaurus, while one tree places it closer to Anodontosaurus. The genus Zuul lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
